content.comment_body: Hello, are there any impedance concerns when connecting proximity switches to the 230 input units? If issues occur, can adding resistance in parallel with the input help? Regards, [user_name]

Hi, are you trying to connect a 2-wire sensor? You need to install a capacitor between N and your input. Suggested part number is [article_no] or use an X-capacitor rated at 2.5KV 100nF. This advice is from the relevant section of the [product_name] manual about connecting inputs. Hope this helps, [user_name]

Hi, I've also experienced issues with capacitance sensors. For the past 10 years, I've been using resistors in parallel with the inputs of [product_name] devices, and this method always works for me. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for information and proven methods for connecting proximity and capacitance sensors to [product_name] 230 input units. They discuss concerns about impedance and confirm that using resistors in parallel with the inputs is an effective solution. References to official manuals and compatible components suggest users find current documentation lacking in practical guidance for these scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward instructions and reliable compatibility details for connecting proximity or capacitance sensors to [product_name] 230 input units. They also want official guidance on managing impedance for proper functionality.
